summary: Exhaustive Q4 review completed over the packet-authorized solver-visible contract, verifier, instruction policy, delegated/layout/state interfaces, F2P/P2P boundaries and public CLI surface. The rebuild is not bidirectionally aligned: multiple material work-request requirements are untested or only partially tested, several verifier assertions impose private/internal labels or schema semantics not discoverable from the solver-visible contract, COMP-3 sign acceptance is grading-relevant but underspecified, and instruction.md violates the current instruction shape/path contract. All required walks and a second adversarial omission sweep were completed.

evidence.observation: Q4 requires complete forward/reverse matrices, instruction/document boundary, F2P/P2P, output-interface and second-pass omission walks; material phantom tests, untested requirements and grading-relevant ambiguity require REVISE.

instruction.md must contain the complete material work request, use <=2 short paragraphs or <=20 concise bullets, name required paths, and avoid leaving grading-relevant behavior to private implementation details.

The instruction names broad requirement families and four required CLI commands, but does not define several exact internal labels/schema constraints graded by tests; it is four prose paragraphs and refers to bin/equiv-eval relatively.

The verifier contains 30 F2P-style internal API assertions plus 4 P2P assertions covering COMP-3, layout/framing, restart, policy, accounting, reconciliation, publication and DB uniqueness; it never invokes the public CLI.
Verifier execution is only pytest /tests; no stable CLI command or end-to-end command-line output/failure interface is exercised.
The supplied layout exposes COMP-3 fields, ODO metadata and REDEFINES geometry but does not define the verifier's exact signed/unsigned sign-nibble acceptance or exception vocabulary.
Documented controls are processed_count, accepted_count, rejected_count, effect_count, net_quantity and net_value; no unbalanced_transfers control name is documented.
The inherited schema does not declare UNIQUE(generation_id,sequence) for processed_movements or rejects although verifier tests require duplicate-generation-sequence rejection.
The inherited public CLI has init-db, describe-layout, identity and run with stable arguments and JSON/exit behavior, but those interfaces are not exercised by the verifier.
Operator log provides current-state cutover evidence including decode, checkpoint and reconciliation phases.

Solver-visible handoff states that cutover is blocked on Python equivalence and names the major invariant families, supporting the instruction's current-state premise without supplying the verifier's private labels.

findings.criterion: Complete forward requirement -> verifier coverage; stable public CLI/path interfaces
findings.why_it_matters: The work request explicitly requires preserving init-db, describe-layout, identity and run and honoring caller-supplied source/layout paths, but the verifier never invokes bin/equiv-eval. The only alternate-layout test calls load_layout directly, and no test proves --source/--layout propagation, command JSON shape, required arguments, or run exit/failure behavior. A solver can break the documented public interface and still pass.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add behavioral CLI coverage for all four preserved commands and especially run/identity/describe-layout caller-supplied path handling, stable JSON fields and exit behavior. Keep assertions at the documented external interface rather than private implementation structure.
findings.regression_risk: High: CLI plumbing or output regressions can escape grading while internal helpers remain green.

findings.criterion: Reverse verifier -> solver-visible contract alignment; no private labels/return-value contracts
findings.why_it_matters: Multiple tests grade exact internal exception substrings and private issue/control labels (for example padding, digit, sign, negative, outside, layout, fingerprint, QUANTITY, TRANSFER_LOOP, ITEM_INACTIVE and WAREHOUSE_INACTIVE) plus exact RecordDecodeError offset/length fields. The solver-visible contract requests behavioral correctness but does not declare these strings/fields as stable interfaces. Conforming implementations with different internal messages/codes can fail.
findings.minimal_remediation: Either expose only genuinely stable externally consumed error/code/record-boundary contracts in legitimate solver-visible technical documentation, or remove private-string/internal-return assertions and grade observable semantics instead.
findings.regression_risk: High: implementation-equivalent repairs can be rejected solely for private vocabulary or internal exception shape.

findings.criterion: Reverse alignment for database durability/idempotency schema constraints
findings.why_it_matters: The verifier requires duplicate (generation_id, sequence) rejection in both processed_movements and rejects. The solver-visible inherited schema does not contain those uniqueness constraints and the instruction does not state that sequence uniqueness per generation is a required schema invariant. This is a material hidden schema requirement.
findings.minimal_remediation: Make per-generation sequence ownership/uniqueness a legitimate solver-visible state/schema contract if it is required, then test it; otherwise stop grading those undeclared uniqueness choices.
findings.regression_risk: High: a solver preserving the supplied schema and achieving restart idempotency through another conforming mechanism can fail hidden DB constraints.

findings.criterion: Reconciliation contract discoverability and complete control coverage
findings.why_it_matters: The instruction says to reconcile every documented control. legacy.controls documents six controls, but the verifier additionally requires a named unbalanced_transfers reconciliation control that is not documented. Conversely, the suite directly falsifies effect_count but does not independently falsify processed_count, accepted_count, rejected_count, net_quantity and net_value. The reverse direction contains a phantom control and the forward direction does not prove every documented control.
findings.minimal_remediation: Document any required transfer-balance invariant as a legitimate reconciliation contract without leaking test topology, and add independent behavioral mismatch scenarios for each material documented control (grouped naturally where one scenario proves multiple controls).
findings.regression_risk: High: both hidden-extra-control failures and silent omissions of documented controls are possible.

findings.criterion: Forward coverage of durability, atomic accounting, checkpoint/restart and atomic publication requirements
findings.why_it_matters: Several strong operational requirements are only weakly or partially exercised. Successful double-run idempotency does not prove checkpoints are written only after durable DB progress or behavior across a failed/partial transaction. Unit effect calculations and negative-inventory rejection do not prove atomic multi-effect inventory application. Publication tests prove reconciliation gating/idempotency but not atomic visibility under partial publish failure. These are explicit safety/durability requirements that can be violated while current tests pass.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add failure-injection/state-transition tests for transaction rollback vs checkpoint advancement, partial multi-effect application, restart from the last durable boundary, and publication atomicity/no partial visible report set.
findings.regression_risk: High: crash/restart and partial-write defects can survive despite green happy-path/idempotency tests.

findings.criterion: Grading-relevant ambiguity: COMP-3 sign domain and framing failure semantics
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'COMP-3 signs/digits' does not specify the accepted positive sign nibbles or signed-vs-unsigned domain, while the verifier requires signed fields to reject F, unsigned fields to reject C, unsigned packing to use F and signed negative packing to use D. It also grades exact complete-malformed-record boundary reporting without a solver-visible framing failure contract. Two competent implementations can reasonably differ and only one passes.
findings.minimal_remediation: Define the packed-decimal sign-domain and externally required malformed-record boundary semantics in a legitimate record-format/framing contract, or relax tests to accepted COBOL-equivalent representations and observable rejection behavior.
findings.regression_risk: High: otherwise correct packed-decimal/framing implementations can fail due to an unstated dialect choice.

findings.criterion: Instruction-policy shape, completeness and path discoverability
findings.why_it_matters: instruction.md is four prose paragraphs, exceeding the explicit <=2 short-paragraph alternative, and names the public executable as relative bin/equiv-eval despite the absolute-path rule. It also refers generically to documented legacy controls without naming the concrete contract path. For a large_system_strict task the policy expressly allows up to 20 concise bullets so completeness need not be sacrificed.
findings.minimal_remediation: Reshape the work request into <=20 concise functional bullets or <=2 short paragraphs; use /app/equiv/bin/equiv-eval and explicitly reference the legitimate solver-visible layout/control/state contracts needed to discover required behavior.
findings.regression_risk: Medium: remediation must avoid converting the instruction into a hidden-test checklist or moving material goals into prompt-extension docs.

F2P_BOUNDARY_REVIEW.assessment: All 30 substantive F2P tests were traced. Several legitimately target required behavior, but internal message/code contracts, hidden DB uniqueness and the extra reconciliation control lack solver-visible ownership; several external/durability boundaries are bypassed by direct helper tests.

P2P_BOUNDARY_REVIEW.assessment: The four P2P cases have legitimate preservation intent (valid signed COMP-3, active policy, matching reconciliation, first publication) and are not circular self-reported booleans, but the preservation set does not cover the documented public CLI or a full successful dynamic-layout workflow.

OUTPUT_INTERFACE_REVIEW.assessment: No test invokes the stable CLI or validates its JSON schemas/exit codes. Internal exceptions and issue/control labels are instead graded as if stable interfaces without solver-visible declaration.
